title: Stressful Home Insurance Experience
body:
This is connected to my previous post:
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/968622
I am looking to lodge an AFCA complaint but just wondering if there is anything else I should consider? This claim has become non stop mental torture.
I had very stressful run with Everyday insurance for flooring claim.
1) Initially they refused the claim because floating floors were not content and considered them as building though PDS treats it as content. They only accepted a claim after lodgement of complaint and admitted that it was their mistake.
2) Their nominated builder did assessment and stated that they were unable to find matching flooring and full flooring replacement would also require kitchen removal because the flooring runs underneath. They were unable to match flooring. The insurer denied and said only best match would be provided though PDS states matching benefit.
3) The internal assessor was assigned by insurer after another complaint who accepted the claim to replace full flooring based on matching benefit and asked for a quote. When the quote came, they are now refusing to replace flooring under the kitchen stating it falls under the building and they won't do it.
4) As part of the claim decision email, they also sent me an assessor's internal report which had clear notes under recommendation from them to change full flooring including removal of kitchen and they had requested a quote on the same basis. In conclusion section, it was stated that they had approved full flooring. They however also put an estimated cost under the Reserve section. The builder quote came quite higher and it appears they have now intentionally narrowed down the scope to keep pricing closer to what they had estimated under their reserve estimate because the full replacement including kitchen removal based on the quote is higher.
4) I had multiple calls and email exchanges with this assessor where it was always maintained that full flooring would be replaced. They didn't mention at any point that kitchen removal was out of scope. The builder also maintained from the beginning including their own assessment report that the full replacement requires kitchen removal and the assessor was aware of it but never raised any objection plus their recommendation in their own internal report also made the same aspect.
The assessor alteration of decision to match their arbitrary financial reserve is a serious concern.
